requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: structural: `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` has no incoming implementation edges, and the supplied review roots are empty. Each clause states observable harness behavior, not a structural property that needs implementation evidence.

- "every direct implementation reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source selection to the initial mandatory inputs": this fixes which sources appear in the input set. A different internal design could produce the same set, such as one collection pass or a different data structure. Because that alternative still satisfies the text, the design is discretionary.
- "An in-source reference selects its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline; an anchor selects its named file or node": these are selection rules, so they describe outputs. No type, signature or field is prescribed.
- "Source access, exclusions, errors, and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules": this defers to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, which the text cites, and adds no structure of its own.
- "Refining declarations continue to contribute their complete text" and "Implementation helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively": both describe what is supplied and when. Neither names a library, algorithm, interface or ownership relationship.

The text names no signatures, types, fields, ownership or delegation through named interfaces. The requirement has no structural obligations, so it needs no implementation roots.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`.

- **Roots contribute to the mandatory inputs, including when tests exist.** In `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]`, an `:impl:` anchor plus an in-source `{impl}` reference yields a `src/lib.rs` input.
  - Adding a `{test}` reference keeps the `fn[api]` root in the inputs.
  - A `:test:` anchor also keeps the implementation root.
  - An `:impl:` anchor with no in-source reference is still enough.
  - `fn[removing_either_root_changes_the_evidence_but_keeps_both_checks]` covers all four impl/test combinations. The structural prompt's subject contains `api.md` exactly when the `:impl:` anchor exists, whatever the tests do.
- **Selection of the enclosing node or the whole file.** The first test asserts the single `src/lib.rs` input has item `fn[api]`. It contains `helper();` but not `fn helper`, so the selection is the enclosing node and no helper is supplied. A later scenario has an unanchored in-source reference and asserts `unanchored.mandatory_inputs() == inputs`. A plain-text root, `src/details.txt`, is supplied whole with item `""` and its full text. The `:impl: api.md` anchor selects the named file. Anchors that name a node are covered by `#fn[api]`.
- **Source access, exclusions and errors.** `fn[structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules]` covers three cases. A `.gitignore`d root fails with an "excluded" error. A missing node selector `fn[missing]` fails with an error naming it. An anchor into `evidence/generated.rs` is allowed and supplied, per the existing mandatory-input rules.
- **Deduplication.** The anchor and the reference to the same node produce exactly one input.
- **Refining declarations contribute complete text.** A refining requirement with a two-paragraph body is supplied, and the assertions check both "Complete refinement." and "Second paragraph.".
- **Helpers not supplied recursively.** This is the `fn helper` absence assertion above.
- **Scope limits.** An example and a distributed requirement both get no review roots, which matches the "non-distributed requirement" scope.

The assertions would fail on the plausible violations: skipping roots when tests exist, supplying a whole file for a node selection, supplying duplicates, dropping refining text, or bypassing the access checks.

Second assessment `false`: Add a test, marked {test}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`, in which a non-distributed requirement has NO `:impl:` anchor. The implementation should be only an in-source {impl} reference, placed on an outline node such as `fn[api]` in `src/lib.rs`. Do this both with and without an incoming {test} reference. Assert that `AssessmentSources::prepare(...).mandatory_inputs()` contains exactly that enclosing node (`item == "fn[api]"`) and that `review_roots` is set. Add a second case where the {impl} reference is in a file with no language outline, such as `notes.txt`. Assert that the whole file is selected (`item == ""`). — The requirement says every direct in-source {impl} reference contributes its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when there is no outline. The marked tests `structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest`, `removing_either_root_changes_the_evidence_but_keeps_both_checks` and `structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules` always declare an `:impl:` anchor next to the in-source reference. The reference and anchor deduplicate to the same `fn[api]` selection. An implementation that read only anchors and ignored in-source {impl} references would pass all of them. The no-outline whole-file rule for in-source {impl} references is not tested at all. `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` covers whole-file selection only for {test} references, and it is not marked for this requirement.

In the refining-declaration case at the end of `structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest`, assert the supplied mandatory inputs. They must include the refining declaration's complete text (`Refinement.`). They must not include a source selection for the {impl} reference that sits inside the declaration. Currently the case only asserts `review_roots.is_some()`. — The requirement says refining declarations continue to contribute their complete text, and that only references outside a declaration contribute source selections. The existing test checks only that review roots exist. It would pass if the refining text were dropped or truncated, or if the in-declaration reference were treated as a source root.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.

output.rationale:
`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` has no implementation edges or roots. Its clauses specify only observable behavior of the mandatory-input set, so no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

- "every direct implementation reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source selection to the initial mandatory inputs": this sets what the input set contains. A harness could build the set with different code and produce the same set, so no library, type or interface is prescribed.
- "An in-source reference selects its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline; an anchor selects its named file or node": these are selection rules about results. They do not say how selection is implemented.
- "Source access, exclusions, errors, and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules": this defers to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, which sets its own behavior. It adds no signature, type or ownership requirement here.
- "Refining declarations continue to contribute their complete text" and "Implementation helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively": both are behavioral statements about what is supplied up front and what is fetched on demand.

The text names no signatures, type or field relationships, ownership, or required delegation through an interface. The incoming `{test}` references do not change this: they supply evidence for the behavior, and no structural property is left unchecked.
